# wallpaper-engine-dsh
English | 中文
A DSH bundle that turns the local **Wallpaper Engine** library into a living background for DSH. Vid
eo wallpapers play behind the chat UI; web wallpapers render directly. Crossfade, liquid-glass panel
s, a readability veil that adapts to the wallpaper, manual framing, rotation lists, search, and a bi
lingual UI live in one dedicated settings section.
## Features
### Wallpaper list

- Lists only types the browser can truly render: video and web wallpapers.
- Scene and application w
allpapers are Wallpaper Engine's private `.pkg` format; the browser cannot execute them, so they are

not listed.
- Every listed wallpaper actually plays, tagged 视频/网页 (video / web).
- The search box f
ilters by title or Workshop ID.
### Dark material and legibility

- The material is permanently dark. Set the shell theme to dark; the dark material assumes it.
- The

veil is always black; even a pitch-black wallpaper cannot swallow the UI.
- The Smart veil samples
the wallpaper's brightness and busyness (the standard deviation of luminance) every few seconds and

strengthens the veil when a scene drifts too bright or too busy.
- Web wallpaper pixels are unreadab

le inside the sandbox, so the Smart veil samples their preview image instead.
- The glass body is sa
mpled from the wallpaper: hue from its average colour, chroma capped at 14%. The body lightens as th

e scene darkens; its alpha follows brightness and busyness together (0.16–0.34).
- The edge is model
led as a lit column: a specular along the top, a bounce along the bottom, darkened side walls, and a

dark outer contour. Edge light strengthens as the wallpaper darkens.
- The specular is static by de
fault; the Pointer highlight setting rides a thin edge glint along the composer's rims with the mous
e (a 6px top band plus a fainter bottom bounce, never deeper than 6px into the face, dimming as the

pointer sinks; repaints each frame, off by default).
- When the composer floats over bright content,
an inner dimming layer rises to a 35% ceiling (the HIG value for this case).
### Refraction
- Each pane rasterises its displacement map at its own pixel size and radius; `feDisplacementMap` si

ts at the head of the filter chain — refract first, then blur.
- Displacement peaks at the rim and d
ecays inward to zero. The edges compress the scene inward; this is where the liquid read comes from.

- A ResizeObserver rebuilds the map when a pane changes size.
- The Surface refraction setting turn

s the whole lens layer off — plain backdrop blur remains.
- Refraction renders in Chromium-family en
gines only (see Limitations).
### Tiers and coverage
| Tier | Surfaces | Blur cap |

| T1 | Crop-adjust bar | 4px |
| T2 | Composer, menus, dock, new-session button | 10px |
| T3 | Sett
ings dialog, full-page workbenches | 14px |
- Glass belongs to the control layer: message bubbles keep only body and edge light, with no backdro

p capture; settings cards soften to a translucent token fill.
- Menus, dialogs, overlay panels and t

he dock take their own tier; submenus (`role="menu"`) take T2.
- Tooltips take the body tint and the

bevel, with no backdrop capture.
[该节后续省略]
### Manual framing

1. Pick the base arrangement under 排布: fill, contain, fill-stretch, native, free.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
The bundle has two halves:
- **Host plugin**: discovers the Wallpaper Engine install (Steam registry keys, `libraryfolders.vdf`
, standard Windows/macOS/Linux paths), enumerates the default projects, my projects and Workshop dir

ectories, keeps only browser-renderable types, and serves data over same-origin routes:
- `GET /we-b

ackground/inventory[?refresh=1]`
- `GET /we-background/media/<token>[/<entry file or sub-resource>…]
` — HTTP Range supported, so video seeking works. A web wallpaper's URL points straight at its entry
file; relative references inside the wallpaper resolve per Wallpaper Engine's own rules. Media resp

onses carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so sandboxed iframes can read their own resources.
- `

GET /we-background/preview/<token>`
- **Browser plugin**: renders the selected wallpaper on a fixed
layer below the app frame and contributes the settings UI. Every effect reads DSH design tokens.
Media service hardening:
- Tokens are unguessable 72-bit random values; they stay stable across inventory rebuilds and regene

rate only on an explicit refresh.
- Sub-resource paths pass a lexical containment check, then a real

-filesystem recheck; symlinks cannot point outside the wallpaper directory.
- HTML and SVG responses

carry a `sandbox` CSP and cannot execute as the DSH origin.
- Wallpaper iframes pin a neutral `colo

r-scheme`; the shell's dark theme cannot leak into third-party wallpapers.
- The CORS wildcard only
lets the token holder read files it could already request; the whole service listens on loopback onl

y.
- Truncated-length responses terminate instead of ending silently short.
- The inventory caches f

or 30 seconds on the host; install discovery runs off the request path and caches for 10 minutes.
-
The plugin registers no model tools and occupies no prompt.
## Limitations
- Scene and application wallpapers are not listed: they are Wallpaper Engine's private `.pkg` packag

es, which a browser cannot execute.
- Web wallpapers are storage-isolated; wallpapers that save stat

e across loads cannot keep it.
- Web wallpapers with sound stay silent until you interact with the p
age (sandboxed audio autoplay rules); wallpapers depending on Wallpaper Engine's system audio input

have no signal to draw.
- Video codecs follow the browser's decoder support: H.264, VP8, VP9 and AV1
play directly; H.265/HEVC cannot software-decode on most machines. When a video claims to play but
decodes no frames, it is marked undecodable and leaves the grid; the verdict sticks to that file (si
ze + mtime), so a re-encoded file is picked up automatically on the next refresh. Transcode to an H.

264 mp4 or a VP9 webm for full playback.
- The glass reads DSH design tokens; if a shell refactor re

names them, the glass degrades to a plain translucent fill.
- Surface refraction renders in Chromium
-family engines only: Safari and Firefox parse `backdrop-filter: url()` and then drop the whole chai
n, so the plugin gates it by UA and falls back to plain blur. The Electron desktop is unaffected.
